ai.subject: Pharmacology
ai.summary: Antiretroviral therapy (ART) suppresses HIV replication, restores immune function, and prevents disease progression. Effective lifelong treatment requires selecting drug classes, monitoring response, and managing side effects.

b: Goal: viral load <50 copies/mL after 24 weeks
Start ART in all diagnosed persons, regardless of CD4 count
Regimens are usually 2‑drug (integrase inhibitor + NRTI) or 3‑drug
sections.p: HIV infects CD4+ T‑cells, leading to progressive immune loss. ART combines drugs that target different steps of the viral life cycle to keep viral load undetectable.

b: NRTIs block reverse transcription; backbone of most regimens
Integrase strand transfer inhibitors (INSTIs) prevent viral DNA integration – high barrier to resistance
Protease inhibitors (PIs) inhibit viral maturation – require boosting, many interactions
NNRTIs bind reverse transcriptase – low barrier, avoid if resistance risk
sections.p: Understanding drug classes, resistance barriers, and drug‑drug interactions guides regimen choice and long‑term success.
